narrative: The model estimates an 18.0% chance that you will fail the final year. That does not mean failure is certain; it means about 18 in 100 students with a similar profile would not pass. Because the school treats this level of risk as requiring support, you are required to take remedial courses. The strongest influences in your profile actually reduce your estimated risk. First, your history of past class failures is the most important factor: you have none, matching the passing-student average, and this strongly pushes the prediction toward passing. Second, your intention to continue to higher education—reported by all passing students in the comparison group—also lowers your estimated failure risk. Third, not having attended nursery school has a smaller effect and slightly lowers the model’s failure estimate, although most passing students did attend nursery, so this signal is less intuitive. Other parts of your profile explain why an 18% risk remains: you have 6 absences, above the passing average of 3.78, which can work against you. To improve, focus on consistent attendance, keep using the family educational support you have, and maintain your study routine of 2–5 hours weekly while aiming to increase it if possible. Use the remedial courses as targeted help, especially for turning your low failure probability into a clear pass.
